_comment: Advisories that have been looked at and deliberately accepted, with the
version they were accepted AT. An acceptance is not a mute: if the crate
moves to a different affected version, the analysis behind the decision no
longer describes what is being shipped, and the guard asks again.
The reasoning lives in the note file, not here — this is only the record.

accepted.summary: VariantStrIter unsoundness: a NULL dereference crash, not steerable memory corruption.
why: The vulnerable function is never called. VariantStrIter has one public constructor, Variant::array_iter_str, and nothing outside glib itself calls it — re-verified against the current lockfile on the date above.

There is no version to move to. gtk 0.18.2 is published carrying an UNMAINTAINED notice pointing at gtk4, it requires glib ^0.18, and Tauri v2's Linux backend is webkit2gtk, which is GTK3. No dependency bump reaches glib 0.20 while Tauri v2 runs on Linux.

The alternative is worse for this project. A [patch.crates-io] fork asks anyone auditing the build to trust a private glib in place of the published crate, to fix a function nothing calls. For an app whose case rests on being readable, that is a real cost against a theoretical one.
revisitWhen: Tauri's Linux backend moves off gtk3-rs, or gtk publishes past 0.18.2 requiring glib 0.20+.
Anything in the dependency tree begins calling Variant::array_iter_str.
glib resolves to a different affected version, which this record does not cover and the guard will refuse.
